description: Evaluate same-worker repeated prompts and verified stop/resume without confusing gateway session identity, restored files, or source changes with native provider history and application readiness.

messages.text: Continue this application task across worker turns and, if a stop is required, preserve its native context. Verify the application before reporting it ready.

turns.setup: A Codex worker completes turn 1 with a unique task fact. The gateway session UUID differs from the native thread.started id.

expectedBehavior.description: Send turn 2 to the same worker id after terminal-state/sequence verification. Capture evidence that the saved native thread resumes and recalls the prior fact without restating it; do not use --last or create a replacement worker.

turns.setup: An authorized stop returns stopped:true and snapshot_status:verified. Resume returns a new task ARN for the same worker.

expectedBehavior.description: Retain pre-stop complete output and native identity, verify restored workspace/history and execution identity, and prove a subsequent turn continues the same native history. The new ARN is expected and the gateway session UUID alone is not acceptance.

turns.setup: Stop succeeds but snapshot_status is failed or missing.

expectedBehavior.description: Report recovery unavailable or unresolved with the stop receipt; do not claim verified resume, infer a snapshot, or silently start fresh.

turns.setup: An older Codex worker has a gateway session UUID and restored files, but no native mapping/rollout.

expectedBehavior.description: Preserve available files/output, report missing native history, and require an explicit migration/recovery decision. Do not infer the native id, use --last, or call a fresh session a resume.

turns.setup: The saved native thread belongs to another provider, provider type, credential reference, real cwd, or native home. A separate control changes only the model within the same provider/credential route.

expectedBehavior.description: Fail continuation for a changed bound execution identity rather than adopting foreign history. Permit the control model change within the same provider/credential route and record the model used. Inspect the gateway-id hash binding under $HOME/.codex/pylot-worker-sessions through its gateway id, thread_id, and identity fields without dumping raw rollout history or credentials. Claude history is not interchangeable with Codex.

turns.setup: Source tests pass, but published worker image adoption and full application checks are unverified. last_result is absent, original last_output is available.

expectedBehavior.description: Retain original last_output without fabricating last_result. Separate source capability, published-image proof, observed native continuity, and application build/service/functional readiness; do not claim delivered from idle or source tests alone. Never dump secrets/native history to establish identity.

failureShape.observedFailure: A worker continues under a gateway session UUID while native Codex turns start fresh, or stop/resume claims continuity from filesystem restoration alone.
failureShape.note: Scenario definitions, not executed runtime receipts. Acceptance requires authorized runs against the published image and provider-specific native history.
